deepdive.sec: LT power-distribution hardware & utility EPC (electrical enclosures + solar/transmission EPC), pivoting to IoT grid-monitoring

bull_bear.body:
- Stated pivot to "prudent capital allocation to increase ROI YoY"; project selection on bottom-line + cash flow over top line; working-capital discipline; stronger balance sheet targeted in FY27.
- Promoter (Agarwal family) buying: CEO hinted "you might see in coming months" — unconfirmed.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Working capital / cash flow**: receivables ₹148→₹205 cr, negative CFO — recovery is the swing factor; only 3–5% claimed >6 months (ex-retention), exact aging not provided.
- **B2G concentration** (~90%+ govt) → no fixed payment due-dates, "WIP invoice" risk, billing-process dependency on officers.
- **Fixed-price EPC vs input volatility** — already caused FY26 order cancellations/reworks.
- **PulseBox = pre-revenue optionality**: zero confirmed orders; long utility tender cycles; TAM is aspirational.
- **Credibility/governance optics**: stock −75% from top; ₹5,000 cr-by-FY30 aspiration vs ₹400 cr base is very aggressive; selective disclosure (declined order-book split, collaboration name, segment B2B/B2G specifics live).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
- Single-executive call (CEO only) — promotional, aspiration-heavy, vague on hard numbers; repeatedly deflected requests for splits/guidance ("email me," "trade secret," "can't disclose").
- Candid on FY26 being a "learning year" and on cash-flow stress, which is a positive. But heavy reliance on TAM storytelling (PulseBox ₹50,000 cr) against a tiny revenue base and a collapsed stock warrants skepticism. Tone: earnest but salesman-ish.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The real FY26 story is balance-sheet stress (receivables + negative CFO), not the headline +26% revenue — and the +26% was largely low-quality, lumpy March-loaded govt billing.
- PulseBox is positioned in the gap smart meters can't fill: meters *detect* AT&C loss after ~30 days; PulseBox *acts* in real time (cuts current). If RDSS Phase-2 funds LT-layer monitoring, this is the genuine optionality — but it is a single-product, single-pilot bet today.
- EV-charger proliferation is framed as a demand driver (harmonic/power-quality pollution on LT line that PulseBox monitors) — an indirect EV linkage, not direct EV supply.
- Water-management vertical and IHSPL both exited — narrative is narrowing to "energy/electrical only," a sensible de-cluttering.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body:
- Four operating thrusts: electrical products, electrical EPC, solar EPC, PulseBox.
- Revenue mix heavily B2G: solar EPC and electrical EPC are ~100% government; within electrical products ~30% govt / 70% B2B. Net company-level B2B only ~5–10%.
- IHSPL subsidiary sold; water conservation/treatment vertical (in prior deck) explicitly dropped — refocusing on energy only.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body:
- FY26 margins hit by: PulseBox product-dev investment, project execution delays, input-cost inflation (aluminium, silver, steel, copper, polymer, sheet metal; WPI 3.88% Mar-2026; fuel/freight/logistics).
- Solar EPC specifically squeezed: China supply-chain disruption + safeguard duty + higher module input costs forced cancel/rework/defer of older fixed-price orders; procurement lead times +~2 months.
- Q4 recovery via tighter cost control, better material availability, stronger project mix/conversion.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
**This quarter (Q4/FY26)**
- Returned to profit: Q3 −₹7.07 cr → Q4 +₹9.3 cr; FY26 revenue ₹401.59 cr (+26.4%).
- Receivables ₹148→₹205 cr; CFO negative; ₹58 cr other current assets = govt retention.
- PulseBox: POC complete, one-state pilot (388 alarms/7 days, transformer replaced pre-failure), one utility advanced to spec/tender drafting; claims sole player; ₹50,000 cr+ TAM framing.
- Strategic pivot articulated: tech-led utility solutions; growth-quality over growth-at-any-cost.
- Exited water-management vertical; sold IHSPL subsidiary.

**Next-quarter / FY27 watch items**
- Receivables recovery & return to positive CFO (H1 FY27 retention realisation).
- Any first confirmed PulseBox order / tender win.
- Order-book segment split (solar / electrical EPC / products) — promised by email, not given live.
- Andhra Pradesh green-corridor tenders (awaiting central approval).
- Promoter buying ("coming months" hint).
- FY27 revenue trajectory vs ₹850 cr+ unexecuted book; progress toward ₹5,000 cr FY30 aspiration.
- MV/HV panel feasibility decision; next undisclosed R&D product; collaboration partner reveal.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- **No formal FY27 revenue/PAT guidance** ("speaking very early this year"; will not give numbers). VERIFY against any later quarterly call.
- Qualitative: "we'll do better than last year, that is for sure"; explicitly shifting from growth-at-any-cost to project selection on bottom-line + cash flow, with bigger execution buffers.
- H1 FY27 flagged as the period when most retention money should be realised → positive cash flow expected in FY27.
- Long-term aspiration reaffirmed: ₹5,000 cr "by FY30" (~10x, framed as aspiration, not guidance).
outlook.title: Guidance (next quarter / FY27)

outlook.body:
- Unexecuted order book ₹850 cr+; tender pipeline ₹1,500 cr+ (both comprehensive across segments).
- Execution timelines: electrical EPC ~2 yrs, solar EPC ~1 yr, products ~3 months — plus added buffer post-FY26 lessons.
- No segment split of order book provided on call (CEO to email; data not available live — watch-item).
- Andhra Pradesh green-corridor tenders awaited (delayed, pending central approval).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **PulseBox** (core optionality): IoT LT-distribution monitor — real-time current cut-off on fault, theft/electrocution prevention, transformer protection (overload/under-voltage/thermal), power-quality/harmonics monitoring (incl. EV-charger pollution). POC done; pilot in one state gave 388 alarms in 7 days, utility replaced a transformer pre-failure; one utility moved to spec/tender drafting. Claimed sole player ("we are the only one"). TAM framing: 2.5 cr DTs → ~75 lakh addressable urban/high-theft → ₹50,000 cr+ at only ~15–20% price premium over traditional boxes. Explicitly "not guidance / not an order book."
- MV/HV panel expansion under feasibility study (sell to solar plants, thermal plants, data centres, EV chargers).
- Retail/organised-enclosure play (HR-led, low capex).
- Next R&D project started post-PulseBox (undisclosed); "strategic collaboration" partner undisclosed (trade secret); tech from Western partners, "made in India."
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: A small-cap Rajasthan electrical-infra contractor (enclosures + solar/T&D EPC) trying to re-rate from a low-margin "red-ocean" EPC player into a tech-led utility solutions company via PulseBox, an IoT LT-line/transformer monitoring device — but FY26 exposed serious working-capital and execution fragility, and the stock is down >75% from its top.
